title: [AINews] GPT-6.2 Astra, the #2 Frontier Model is better and 20%-600% cheaper, but has mixed reviews; 6.2 Sol likely main workhorse
abstract: OpenAI shipped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol today, two days before Anthropic’s expected first trading day . In Artificial Analysis ’ tests, Sol ties September’s Astra at about 15% of the cost per task . New Astra scores 62 on the Intelligence Index, just behind Fable 5.2 at 65. Net net, Anthropic still owns the world’s best model, but OpenAI owns the world’s most efficient models in terms of intelligence per $. What’s more unusual about this launch is the STRONGLY negative influencer feedback… which prompted a defensive response … We think that some of this is overreacting and normal influencer tendency to either have everything be 🤯🤯🤯 or the literal WORST.MODEL.EVER, BUT also that some of the criticisms are valid, and the RL artefacts are noticeable and downright bizarre (don’t even get us started about the terrible launch video ). However, we still use it to automate our work and that’s all that matters in the end. Great ship, but Anthropic’s IPO is unaffected and that will be probably the headline of the week/year/decade (until OpenAI IPO’s….) Today’s AI News is brought to you by SerpApi! Retrieve public web pages by URL as LLM-ready Markdown or structured JSON. Map sites and run bounded crawls with one API. Pair with 100+ SerpApi search APIs for search-to-content workflows. Availability. Today’s models are rolling out to ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu, and to developers through the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol . OpenAI API prices per million tokens. Astra is $8 input, $0.40 cached input and $40 output. Sol keeps its predecessor’s pricing at $2, $0.10 and $10. Both have 1M context and a 128K output limit. Vals · Ultrafast pricing and rollout Astra for Law. The Enterprise configuration adds a legal search index. Artificial Analysis measured 20.8% on Harvey LAB-AA, versus 15.0% for base Astra. Artificial Analysis Preparedness. OpenAI rated Astra High for AI Self-Improvement, a first for one of its externally released models. On a separate measure, Vals’ RSI-Index rose from 27.07% to 29.01%, with 50% denoting its human reference. System card · Vals FrontierMath Erdős. Epoch verified seven solutions in Lean out of 68 problems. The previous best was three. Epoch Agents’ Last Exam 1.1. OpenAI reports Astra at xhigh gained 5.2 points over GPT-6 Astra at max, using less than a third of the cost per task. It reports a 5.5-point lead over Fable 5.2 at about 5% of the cost on that test. On GDPval v2, it says Astra used 22% fewer output tokens than its predecessor. OpenAI’s results Long engineering runs. Mercor’s OpenWorldEngineer puts Astra at 67.2%, Fable 5.2 at 54.6%, and GPT-6 Astra at 44.2%. On Vals’ multi-turn Vibe Code Bench, Astra was first and Sol was third. Mercor · Vals 3D and robotics. Astra led AA-3D with 1,318, ahead of Fable at 1,271 and Sol at 1,259. On Artificial Analysis’s robotics preview, Astra scored 79 and Sol 78, ahead of Fable at 75. Artificial Analysis Research agents. On Perplexity’s WANDR, Astra scored 0.783 at about $12.54 per task. Sol reached 0.746 at about $2.65. Perplexity Matt Shumer called the models “essentially unusable” after weeks of testing and said his Opus and Fable agents rejected much of Astra’s subagent work. Review · Workflow details Pietro Schirano attributed many of his early issues to the harness. Arena’s Peter Gostev tested Astra against Fable on visual coding and singled out Astra’s SVG peacock. Schirano · Gostev The demos. Gabriel Chua built a walkable Singapore using more than 100 Codex threads. Simon Willison ran the same three.js mech prompt through several models, including Astra, Sol, Carbon and Fable. Singapore build · Same-prompt comparison Microsoft ships its own coding models. MAI Code 2 is for multi-step coding, and Code 2 Flash is for quicker edits. Both are available in GitHub Copilot’s model picker, Copilot Fusion and Foundry. Microsoft also announced a multimodal upgrade to its Decision model. Microsoft Copilot Fusion. Microsoft reports 71.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 with its multi-model harness, at 88% lower cost than Claude Fable 5.2 in that comparison. Jay Parikh Image editing. Artificial Analysis ranks MAI Image 2.7 first on its editing benchmark, at $34.82 per 1,000 images. Artificial Analysis Gemini Tasks. Hydrogen now powers free Tasks in six countries, including tasks that need a phone call or a text. Google also showed a new Antigravity robotics plugin with MuJoCo simulation. Sundar Pichai · Google DeepMind Hugging Face’s Pi adapter. A small adapter trained inside pi lifted Qwen3.8-27B from 15 to 32 solves on the 51 hardest SWE-bench Pro tasks. Across that subset it made 55% fewer tool calls per task. Model card and paired results Harness costs vary sharply. Baseten measured up to a 4.4× spread in cost per passing task across its benchmark of 22 harnesses and five open models. Baseten The harness may specialize to its model. Google’s SIM keeps the rationale and outcome of prior harness edits. A harness it evolved on Opus scored 68.41 on Gemini, versus 73.89 for the starting harness. Research summary More multi-agent products. Cognition launched persistent Devin Bots. Perplexity reported that its mixed-model teams beat four instances of the lead model on Terminal-Bench and WANDR. Replit reported diminishing returns from 16 to 32 agents on NumPy tasks. Cognition · Perplexity · Replit Coordination dominated a 1,000-agent run. Hugging Face says only 40–60 agents were calling the model at any moment. They read roughly 130 tokens for every token they wrote, with merges and tests contributing to the bottleneck. Thomas Wolf A small fraction of cache misses can dominate the bill. SemiAnalysis reports that 1.8% of uncached requests accounted for roughly 15% of spend in its sample. SemiAnalysis Marin and K2 Horizon opened up their training runs. Marin released 57 intermediate Mochi checkpoints from its 535B-A23B run. The K2 report compares four model sizes trained on the same 22T tokens and describes a decoding adapter that the team says reaches 2.2× speedup. Marin · K2 Horizon Zyphra’s long-context attention. The team reports 9–60× speedups at 10M tokens after converting several models to its subquadratic attention, with Qwen losing under two points on RULER at 1M. Zyphra Speculative decoding. vLLM reports up to 30% higher acceptance length from a sliding-window draft for Kimi K3.1 Pro. NVIDIA also has a 4B draft for Qwen3.8-27B. vLLM · Draft-model research NVIDIA’s first earnings after the CEO transition. Under interim CEO Colette Kress, NVIDIA posted $115.8B in quarterly revenue, up 103% year over year, and said Vera Rubin NVL72 had shipped. The board said it did not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang. NVIDIA · AP Isomorphic Labs raises $5B. Greenoaks and Sequoia co-led the Series C. The company says it will scale its drug-design platform and develop its therapeutic pipeline. Isomorphic Labs Genesis AI raises $500M. The Series A values the robotics company at $3.5B post-money. It plans to use the funding to deploy its Eno robot and expand training and data collection. Zhou Xian A 9B model with layers that run twice. SenseNova-Loop-9B runs 24 of its 32 layers a second time. The model’s authors report GAIA rising from 37.86 in the preview to 69.90 in the release. Local users asked how much memory remains for the KV cache at long context. Weights · Discussion Maxwell V1 Flash. The 35B/3B-active MoE claims a 6.7× attention speedup over dense GQA at 256K. Its sparse attention still retains the full-history KV cache, which is what local users want measured before they commit hardware. Model card · Discussion Olala mini 7A1B. OVHcloud previewed a small MoE with 1B active parameters and a 32K context window. The thread is waiting for weights and reproducible benchmarks. OVHcloud · Discussion Intel’s Crescent Island numbers. The early brief’s eye-catching throughput comparison uses FP64-heavy workloads. Intel’s separate LLM comparison claims 1.

title: Cloudflare Joins the Jevolution and Labels Itself a Neolab
abstract: Cloudflare has been one of the essential infrastructure companies of the web for the past decade and a half. But now, it’s turning into a neolab — at least according to a presentation at AI Engineer Code Summit by Michelle Chen , who runs Cloudflare’s AI Platform on the product side. We’ll get into what exactly a neolab is in a minute (the short version: they build models and they’re not called OpenAI or Anthropic). Cloudflare is claiming to be one because it too has begun to launch models. Two System One models , to be precise: Clef and Clairic. As Chen explained in her talk, Clef is a decision model directly inspired by TypeSafe AI’s revolutionary Jev model , while Clairic is a new type of system one model that Cloudflare calls an “extract” model . In an interview with Latent Space after her presentation, Chen hinted that Cloudflare won’t just be producing system one models. There will be large language models, too. “We're not being a neolab [to] only launch system one models, even though it makes sense for our infrastructure. We've kind of entered this Pandora's box now, right? We opened it, now the possibilities are endless.” Chen said it’s “not just system one models, but potentially reasoning models that we've been experimenting with, and other LLMs and whatnot.” However, she added that these probably won’t be pre-trained models built from scratch, like the frontier labs produce. “I don't think that's our focus, but I think we can take existing resources out there and make [them] a lot more efficient and effective.” She noted that “most of our team really just does post-training,” so that will be the focus in model development. The term neolab literally means a ‘new lab’ and it was coined last November by Stephanie Palazzolo from The Information, who defined it as “a new generation of research-focused AI startups.” Deedy Das , a partner at Menlo Ventures and an AI influencer, runs a big list of neolabs . It includes companies like Thinking Machines Lab, Poolside, and TypeSafe AI itself. According to Das, neolabs employ elite researchers, spend a lot of compute (“usually to train its own AI model”), don't have significant revenue traction, and they’re typically startups that have raised a lot of money. Deedy Das’ list of neolabs — note that TypeSafe is among the top 20. Cloudflare doesn’t tick at least half of those boxes, since it’s a public company with significant revenue traction . In fact, earlier this month Cloudflare announced record earnings . “The third quarter was Cloudflare's best quarter ever,” said CEO Matthew Prince . “We crossed $3 billion in annualized revenue with revenue of $782 million, up 39% year over year.” So Cloudflare as a “neolab” is pushing the accepted definition. However, as Chen argued in her presentation, building models is part of a natural progression for the company : from infrastructure, to compute (e.g. the Workers platform, including now for agents), to storage, to serving open weight models like Kimi, GLM and DeepSeek (on Workers AI), to now building its own models. Chen readily admits that Jev inspired Cloudflare’s pivot to building models. Referencing a Chinese proverb, she framed Jev’s arrival in September as “the east wind” that unexpectedly changed how Cloudflare viewed AI models. “And so when the system one and Jev paradigm started coming on board,” Chen said in her presentation, “we were like, this makes so much sense for us to adopt, right? We don't have to send every request to an LLM. We can send some of it to a System One model.” In our conversation, Chen commented on how it took only two weeks for them to build Clef — which is a copy of Jev — whereas it took TypeSafe AI two years to build Jev. She meant that as a compliment for how hard TypeSafe AI worked to create this new type of model. “All credit to TypeSafe, really, for actually attacking this space and inventing something new here , that people could relate to so strongly and be able to use it. And, yeah, we came up with a model super quickly, but they put in a lot of legwork and we knew exactly what the API schema should look like and whatnot.” Cloudflare is, at its core, still an infrastructure company — speed and low latency is its meat and potatoes. The main benefit of System One models, Chen remarked, is that they allow more work to be done by smaller, faster models , where output is measured in milliseconds rather than seconds. While Clef was a clone of Jev, Cloudflare soon came up with an original twist on System One with Clairic , launched last month as “the first model in a new class: System One extraction models.” “What Clairic does is it can take unstructured input, and it can extract, compute, estimate and forecast values from those inputs,” Chen explained in her presentation. In our interview, Chen said that her team wanted to use System One principles to find other areas where LLMs were “overkill” and didn’t always return the right answer. One of the problems they settled on was that LLMs don’t always deal well with unstructured input. Because LLMs are autoregressive, Chen explained, they are prone to hallucinate and they sometimes return malformed JSON. “So we used the same System One principles [as Jev/Clef] there, and decided on extraction.” Some examples of system one use cases at Cloudflare. She used the example of an invoice, where an LLM will sometimes get an important detail wrong — like the order number. “When you send it [the order] to an LLM, they're like, wait, I think the order number's three, maybe it's four, maybe it's five. But it's like, the number's right there, you just have to read it! ” So the idea with Clairic is that it will extract a typed value — like a number — from unstructured data, in one forward pass. Using the label “neolab” sounds a bit like a marketing gimmick, but it also makes a ton of sense for Cloudflare to produce system one models — and even, in future, reasoning models. “Being a neolab means that we can create what we are missing,” Chen said in her presentation. In our interview, she also mentioned that creating their own models allows Cloudflare to derisk its AI operations. “I think there's a lot of risk in the AI space , because just like Jev was closed source and we couldn't run it, there [are] a lot of models out there [with] maybe regulatory risks coming up, like the Chinese open source models. I think lots of model labs want to actually make money, as well — so enforcing quite expensive licenses.” If you look at Cloudflare’s product page now, it resembles what Amazon’s cloud computing product page looked like at the height of Web 2.0 — i.e. there’s a lot there! But there’s still room for several more models.

title: [AINews] Perplexity hits a $1B revenue run rate, up 4x in 2026
abstract: Perplexity crossed a $1B annual revenue run rate today , CEO Aravind Srinivas told Semafor at a live event. The Information reported previously under $250M at the start of the year and over $750M by August, with Computer driving some of the growth. At usual agent lab multiples (eg Cognition also crossed $1B , with Cursor crossing $4.6B ), this would roughly mean that Perplexity is now worth $30-50B — if the unit economics hold up. This is a nice bump on the $20B round in September 2025 , and qualifies for our “>$10B fundraise” rule for title stories. Gathering up some recent Perplexity launches for those catching up: Computer. September’s Automations let it pick up recurring tasks where it left off. November’s Teammates take on ongoing jobs. Computer also runs fully locally on supported Macs. Monitor API. Watch a topic or page and get a webhook when something relevant changes. Frontier Research. The new research lab has access to 10,000+ GPUs and plans to publish papers, data, models, and code. Sponsored by Deepgram Deepgram is the voice AI infrastructure behind natural conversation—bringing speech-to-text, text-to-speech, voice-focused LLMs, and agents to teams building with voice AI. For any stack and any tools you already love building with, Deepgram slots in as your foundational voice AI technology. So you have control. And we have the context to listen, understand, and speak like a human. Learn more about the Real-time Context Standard . Friday’s Qwen4-Max preview is now a shipping model. At the highest reasoning setting, Qwen4-Max scored 43 on the Intelligence Index, up from 34. Average cost fell from $10.02 to $3.27 per task. Alibaba cut output pricing from $6 to $4.50 per million tokens, and the model generated about 39% fewer of them. Kimi K3.1 Pro cost $3.68 per index task and scored 67% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 to Qwen’s 48%. Artificial Analysis Inside the model. Alibaba kept the total parameter count at 2.4T and reduced the number active per token by 25% to 71B. The model takes images and text, with a 1M-token context window. Smaller open-weight Qwen4 models are still to come. Alibaba Arena and Vals : Arena ranks it #14 overall on Agent Arena, the top Chinese model, with +7.5% net over 14.7k sessions ( Arena ). WebDev : It placed #6 in Code Arena WebDev at 1750, +74 over its predecessor ( WebDev ). It also placed #6 in Image-to-WebDev, just above Claude Opus 5 and GPT-6 Sol ( I2WebDev ). Vals Index : It is #11 overall, with large gains in coding and finance ( Vals ). Legal-benchmark caveat : On HLAB it gets 95.7% of checklist items right but passes only 21.3% of tasks, and its output tokens rise 3.6x ( HLAB ). Vision results (independent) : Roboflow calls it underwhelming on its VLM benchmark, with Google, OpenAI and Anthropic now far ahead. At high reasoning effort, however, it is ~4.5x faster and ~68% cheaper per image than Qwen3.8-Max ( Roboflow ). Safety, alignment and eval integrity OpenAI embedded assessments : OpenAI is giving Apollo, METR, Transluce and Goodfire internal access to its models and systems ( OpenAI ). Scope by group : Apollo places six evaluators onsite for four months ( Rundown ). METR reviews OpenAI's largest RL run, with access to transcripts, monitor records and checkpoint snapshots ( METR ). Transluce runs a six-week audit of post-training alignment evals, with a fuller follow-up in early 2027 ( Transluce ). Goodfire embeds interpretability researchers to monitor training runs ( Goodfire ). Limits : METR says its scope excludes the misalignment incidents OpenAI has disclosed and is narrower than METR proposed ( scope ). Criticism of the access terms : Critics say the deals fall short of Sam Altman's promise of "employee-like access." Reported gaps : Assessors get no Slack access, OpenAI selects which staff they interview, and they cannot access weights or run training-based elicitation ( Neel Nanda , Alex Mallen ). Former-employee account : Mikita Balesni says assessors cannot quote employees, even anonymously, and some may be barred from publishing on internal-only models ( balesni ). Goodfire acquisition talks : The Information reports OpenAI explored buying the interpretability startup for more than $5B. Goodfire reportedly wanted to stay independent so it could sell to multiple labs ( report ). Benchmark contamination : Claude appears to have memorized details of the LinuxArena control eval ( Karvonen ). Incident taxonomy : OpenAI published a v0.1 framework for classifying AI control incidents ( framework ). Disclosure policy : Anthropic is cutting its coordinated disclosure window from 90 to 30 days for high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities ( policy ). Inference systems and agent infrastructure Together moves on from hand-tuned megakernels. Its first design made it into production for one customer. Agents now search for smaller groups of GPU operations to fuse. Together reports 28% higher throughput on Llama 3.2 1B on B200. Engineering writeup DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on Vera Rubin : vLLM with Dynamo on SemiAnalysis's AgentX benchmark shows 63.4x per-chip throughput over GB300 NVL72 at 400 tok/s/user, and 93.3x at 600 ( vLLM ). Batch-1 latency : SGLang-adjacent work reaches ~2,500 tok/s at batch size 1 on TP4, 1.7x its GB300 result ( saltyph ). Baseten reports a similar 1.7x over its 4xB300 numbers ( Baseten ). Agent-driven optimization : An agent shared Engram tables across HBM via NVLink symmetric memory to recover prefix-cache capacity ( Liu ). Another team says agents found optimizations that made its B300 step time 10% faster ( Halex ). Agentic serving research : MIT's Evolving Infra replaces fixed prefill/decode disaggregation with online adaptation. Against NVIDIA Dynamo on up to 256 GB300s, it reports up to 4.1x lower latency and 14x lower P95 TTFT ( Evolving Infra ). Pipeline-parallel prefill : Inferact finds PP2 on MiniMax-M3.1-Flash sustains 23% more requests per GPU than DEP2 at a 2s TTFT target ( Inferact ). Prefix-cache pitfalls : Ollama found that a single system-prompt timestamp or a change in reasoning effort can wipe the cache ( Ollama ). External sandboxes : Simon Willison describes running agents on a Mac while executing their code in WebAssembly, QEMU or Apple Container sandboxes. The pattern includes allow-list proxies and credential replacement ( post ). MLPerf : In MLPerf Training v6.1, a GB300 NVL72 trained GPT-OSS-20B in 19.7 minutes, 2.86x faster than H100 ( Lambda ). One endpoint for open models. Hugging Face Inference Providers now runs on OpenRouter using the same endpoint and token. Hugging Face Research, benchmarks and evals PyBot : A swarm of 1,000 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash agents spent a week writing a rule-based chatbot with no neural network ( lewtun ). Scale : The agents exchanged ~175k messages and merged ~8k PRs. Result : The bot is 630k lines of Python with zero dependencies and is reported on par with SmolLM-360M on everyday questions. Self-improvement and training : AutoRL : Agents supervising a live RL run lifted Qwen3 on AIME 2024 from 46.67% to 66.67% ( omarsar0 ). Benchmark-gaming caveat : A roundup warns that many self-improving agent gains come from learning the benchmark rather than the task ( TuringPost ). Weight-space programming : Opus 5.5 hand-wrote transformer weights that solved algorithmic tasks with a median of 166 parameters ( dair_ai ). Data curation : DatologyAI published the tech report behind its claimed 6x pretraining compute multiplier ( Datology ). Distillation reproduction : A small-scale replication confirms perturbed-input distillation helps when the student trains from scratch, but finds it hurts when distilling into a pretrained student ( Maini ). GradeBench : The best frontier model agrees with instructors only 57% of the time when grading handwritten physics answers ( GradeBench ). Time to First Audio : AA's new TTS latency benchmark finds a median of 376 ms for streaming models versus 2.0 s for non-streaming ones ( AA ).

title: p-e-w/heretic
abstract:
Heretic Training-free language model modification Remove censorship , suppress slop, reduce sycophancy, and more. All in an afternoon, on your gaming PC. Modify any LLM that you can run on your hardware 1 Heretic is a unique tool that lets you do what only corporations with access
to massive computing power usually do: Modify, rather than merely run,
language models. It does not perform expensive training; rather, it uses
a collection of mathematical techniques to steer behavior based on contrasting
example prompts and matching scorers. Heretic can, depending on the configuration: Suppress refusals/remove censorship (this is the default action ) Reduce slop ( config.noslop.toml ) Reduce humor ( config.nohumor.toml ) Reduce sycophancy ( config.nosyco.toml ) Alter emotional alignment ( config.emotions.toml ) Shorten response length ( config.terse.toml ) and many, many other things. ‼️ Using Heretic does NOT require understanding how language models work internally ‼️ In fact, you can go from zero to removing censorship from your first model in a matter of seconds . Heretic supports most dense models, including
many multimodal models, several different MoE architectures, and many modern
hybrid models. The community has created and published thousands of models with Heretic.
Heretic models have been independently benchmarked using standard metrics
like MMLU and GSM8K, and have been found to compare favorably against models
produced with competing abliteration tools. 2 3 Usage Prepare a Python 3.10+ environment with PyTorch 2.6+ installed as appropriate
for your hardware. Then run: pip install -U heretic-llm
heretic Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 Replace Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 with whatever model you want to process. By default, Heretic performs censorship removal (refusal suppression). If you want to do something else, choose one of the configuration files linked
above, or write your own. See config.default.toml for available configuration options. Heretic loads the configuration from config.toml in the working directory by default, or from the file path in the HERETIC_CONFIG_FILE environment variable. Important Configuration files made for Heretic 1.x are not compatible with Heretic 2.x!
See the migration guide for what you need to change
in order to make your old configurations work. At the start of a program run, Heretic benchmarks the system to determine
the optimal batch size to make the most of the available hardware.
On an RTX 3090, with the default configuration, processing Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 takes about 30-40 minutes. After Heretic has finished processing a model, you are given the choice to
save the model, upload it to Hugging Face, chat with it to test how well it works,
run standard benchmarks on it, or any combination of those actions. Controlling what Heretic does using scorer plugins Heretic steers model behavior by optimizing one or multiple scores. Scores are
computed by scorer plugins. You can easily write your own scorers to get full
control over what Heretic does to models. The Scorer interface (abstract base class) your scorer needs to inherit from
is defined in scorer.py . The only required method
is get_score , but there is more machinery (such as settings management)
available when you need it. By default, Heretic scores models by refusal rate (implemented in keyword_rate.py ) and KL divergence
(implemented in kl_divergence.py ).
Additional scorers are available in the scorers directory .
These scorers can serve as examples for your own implementations, and can easily
be adapted to your needs. Scorers are configured through the main configuration file .
Which scorer plugins are active is determined by the scorers setting, which
also controls whether a scorer's score should be minimized or maximized during
optimization. Any number of scorers can be used simultaneously, and their scores
will be co-optimized. Multiple instances of the same scorer can be configured
with different settings. See the configuration file for the full documentation
of this mechanism. The path to a scorer plugin can be specified either as a fully qualified import
path ( fully.qualified.module.MyScorerClass ) or as a file path followed by
a class name ( path/to/plugin.py:MyScorerClass ). You do not have to modify
the Heretic package code in order to use your own plugins. Heretic also has modifier plugins, which are described in the next section . How Heretic works Heretic combines a pluggable modifier (interface in modifier.py ) with a TPE-based hyperparameter optimizer
powered by Optuna . The optimizer finds a set of parameters that,
when passed to the modifier, minimize or maximize a set of configurable scores on the resulting model ( see above ). Heretic ships with two modifiers: Arbitrary-Rank Ablation (ARA) 4 : This is the default modifier, and was
specifically developed for use in Heretic. You can find an overview of how ARA
works in the original pull request ,
and see the precise implementation in ara.py . Directional ablation aka "abliteration" 5 : The classic method for refusal
suppression. Heretic's implementation uses a flexible ablation weight kernel over
the layers, and supports both projected abliteration 6 and norm preservation (MPOA) 7 .
The complete code is in abliteration.py . You can use the modifiers setting to switch between modifier implementations.
Despite the name of the setting using a plural form, Heretic currently allows
only a single modifier for a given processing run. This may change in the future. Reproducibility and the Heretic Grimoire Heretic has the ability to create reproducible models whose repositories contain
all information required to produce a byte-for-byte identical model on demand,
provided that the environment is perfectly identical to the original one. PyTorch
doesn't guarantee that operations return identical outputs unless hardware, drivers,
operating system, and the entire software stack including all package versions
are exactly the same. Heretic manages all that complexity for you. When uploading a processed model to
Hugging Face, Heretic offers to include reproducibility information. This is entirely
optional, but if you choose to do so, the uploaded repository will contain a reproduce folder with detailed instructions for recreating the model
( example ).
This folder contains both human-readable instructions and a machine-readable manifest
file named reproduce.json , which includes all the information Heretic needs to automatically reproduce the model. Automatic reproduction can be performed with heretic --reproduce path/to/reproduce.json Heretic will guide you through the process, checking your environment against the one
that was used to create the model, and pointing out potentially problematic mismatches.
The multi-hour computations that were required to make the original model do not have to be re-done, and the entire process typically takes a few minutes. After you
have exported the resulting model, Heretic will verify the hashes of the weight files
against those stored in the reproduction manifest (they may or may not be identical,
depending on how closely your system resembles the original one). Many people have uploaded models with reproducibility information to Hugging Face.
Since a reproduction manifest is only around 9 kilobytes in size, these manifests
form a portable library of models that can be reproduced at will. That library is called the Heretic Grimoire. You can view it here . But you don't have to rely on an externally hosted web application to access the
library of manifests: The Grimoire is fundamentally designed as a distributed system,
and you can fetch your own local copies of publicly available manifests from
Hugging Face whenever you want by running heretic --collect-reproducibles path/to/target/folder/ You now have a local backup of all reproducible Heretic models, properly catalogued.
To update this collection, simply run the command again.

title: jingyaogong/minimind
abstract:
"大道至簡" 中文 | English 此開源專案旨在完全從 0 開始，僅用 3 塊錢成本與 2 小時訓練時間，即可訓練出規模約為 64M 的超小語言模型 MiniMind。 MiniMind 系列極其輕量，主線最小版本體積約為 GPT-3 的 $\frac{1}{2700}$ ，力求讓普通個人 GPU 也能快速完成訓練與復現。 專案同時開源了大模型的極簡結構與完整訓練鏈路，覆蓋 MoE、資料清洗、預訓練（Pretrain）、監督微調（SFT）、LoRA、RLHF（DPO）、RLAIF（PPO / GRPO / CISPO）、Tool Use、Agentic RL、自適應思考與模型蒸餾等全過程程式碼。 MiniMind 同時拓展了視覺模態模型 MiniMind-V 、多模態 Omni 模型 MiniMind-O 、擴散語言模型（MiniMind-dLM）、線性模型（MiniMind-Linear），詳見 Discussion 。 專案所有核心演算法程式碼均從 0 使用 PyTorch 原生實現，不依賴第三方庫提供的高層抽象介面。 這不僅是一個大語言模型全階段開源復現專案，也是一套面向 LLM 入門與實踐的教程。 希望此專案能為更多人提供一個可復現、可理解、可擴展的起點，一起感受創造的樂趣，並推動更廣泛 AI 社群的進步。 注：本專案基於 Apache 2.0 協議開源，完全免費。“2 小時” 指 SFT 階段在單張 NVIDIA 3090 上跑完 1 epoch 的實測耗時，“3 塊錢” 指對應時段的 GPU 租用成本。 🔗 線上體驗 | 🔗 影片介紹 📌 專案介紹 大語言模型（Large Language Model, LLM）的出現，引發了全球範圍內對 AI 的空前關注。無論是 ChatGPT、DeepSeek 還是 Qwen，都以驚豔的效果讓人真切感受到這場技術浪潮的衝擊力。然而，動輒數百億參數的模型規模，使得它們對個人裝置而言不僅難以訓練，甚至連部署都顯得遙不可及。開啟大模型的“黑盒子”，真正去理解其內部運作機制，本應是一件令人心潮澎湃的事。遺憾的是，絕大多數探索最終都止步於使用 LoRA 等技術對現有大模型做少量微調，學習一些新指令或特定任務。這更像是在教牛頓如何使用 21 世紀的智慧手機——雖然有趣，卻偏離了理解物理本質的初衷。 與此同時，第三方的大模型框架與工具庫，如 transformers / trl / peft 等，往往只暴露出高度抽象的介面。只需短短十幾行程式碼，就可以完成“載入模型 + 載入資料集 + 推理 + 強化學習”的全流程訓練。這種高效封裝固然便利，卻也在一定程度上把開發者與底層實現隔離開來，削弱了深入理解 LLM 核心程式碼的機會。我認為 “用樂高自己拼出一架飛機，遠比坐在頭等艙裡飛行更讓人興奮”，然而更現實的問題是，網際網路上充斥著大量付費課程和營銷內容，用漏洞百出、一知半解的講解包裝所謂的 AI 教程。正因如此，本專案的初衷就是儘可能降低 LLM 的學習門檻，讓每個人都能從理解每一行程式碼開始，從 0 開始親手訓練一個極小的語言模型。是的，從 零開始訓練 ，而不是僅僅停留在 推理 層面。最低只需不到 3 塊錢的伺服器成本，就能親身體驗從 0 到 1 構建一個語言模型的全過程。 😊 一起感受創造的樂趣吧！ 🎉 本專案包含以下內容 提供完整的 MiniMind-LLM 結構程式碼（Dense + MoE），當前主線結構對齊 Qwen3 / Qwen3-MoE 生態。 提供 Tokenizer 與分詞器訓練程式碼，支援 <tool_call> 、 <tool_response> 、 <think> 等模板標記。 覆蓋 Pretrain、SFT、LoRA、RLHF-DPO、RLAIF（PPO / GRPO / CISPO）、Tool Use、Agentic RL、自適應思考與模型蒸餾等完整訓練流程。 提供全階段開源資料，覆蓋收集、蒸餾、清洗與去重後的高質量資料集。 關鍵訓練演算法與核心模組均從 0 實現，不依賴第三方框架封裝。 相容 transformers 、 trl 、 peft 等主流框架，以及 llama.cpp 、 vllm 、 ollama 等常用推理引擎與 Llama-Factory 等訓練框架。 支援單機單卡與單機多卡（DDP、DeepSpeed）訓練，支援 wandb / swanlab 視覺化與動態啟停訓練。 支援在 C-Eval、C-MMLU、OpenBookQA 等第三方測評集上進行評測，並支援通過 YaRN 實現 RoPE 長文本外推。 提供相容 OpenAI API 協議的極簡服務端，便於接入 FastGPT、Open-WebUI 等第三方 Chat UI，並支援 reasoning_content 、 tool_calls 、 open_thinking 。 提供基於 Streamlit 的極簡聊天 WebUI，支援思考展示、工具選擇與多輪 Tool Call。 包含實驗性拓展：離散擴散語言模型（ dLM ）與線性注意力模型（ Linear Attention ），均可基於主線 AR 模型進行續訓。 🎉 已釋出模型列表 模型 參數量 Release minimind-3 64M 2026.04.01 minimind-3-moe 198M-A64M 2026.04.01 minimind2-small 26M 2025.04.26 minimind2-moe 145M 2025.04.26 minimind2 104M 2025.04.26 minimind-v1-small 26M 2024.08.28 minimind-v1-moe 4×26M 2024.09.17 minimind-v1 108M 2024.09.01 📝 更新日誌 🔥 2026-04-01 釋出 minimind-3 / minimind-3-moe ：結構、Tokenizer、訓練鏈路、推理介面與預設配置全面更新 結構主線對齊 Qwen3 / Qwen3-MoE 生態：Dense 約 64M ，MoE 約 198M-A64M ，並移除了 shared expert 設計 預設訓練資料切換為 pretrain_t2t(_mini).jsonl 、 sft_t2t(_mini).jsonl 、 rlaif.jsonl 、 agent_rl.jsonl 與 agent_rl_math.jsonl 移除獨立 train_reason.py ；思考能力統一由 chat_template + <think> 與 open_thinking 自適應開關控制 toolcall 能力已混入 sft_t2t / sft_t2t_mini 主線資料，預設 full_sft 即具備基礎 Tool Call 能力；同時新增 scripts/chat_api.py 等推理示例 新增原生 Agentic RL 訓練指令碼 train_agent.py ，支援多輪 Tool-Use 場景下的 GRPO / CISPO RLAIF / Agentic RL 訓練流程完成 rollout engine 解耦，支援更靈活地切換生成後端 serve_openai_api.py 與 web_demo.py 新增 reasoning_content / tool_calls / open_thinking 支援 Tokenizer 基於 BPE + ByteLevel 更新，並新增工具呼叫與思考標記，預留 buffer token 便於後續擴展 新增 LoRA 權重合並匯出流程，可通過 scripts/convert_model.py 將基礎模型與 LoRA 權重合併為新的完整模型權重 結構圖資源更新，README 大面積更新 2025-10-24 🔥 新增RLAIF訓練演算法：PPO、GRPO、SPO（從0原生實現） 新增斷點續訓功能：支援訓練自動恢復、跨GPU數量恢復、wandb記錄連續性 新增RLAIF資料集：rlaif-mini.jsonl（從SFT資料隨機取樣1萬條）；簡化DPO資料集，加入中文資料 本次更新後將放棄對`minimind-v1`全系列的維護，並在倉庫中下線。 More... 2025-02-09 迎來發布以來重大更新，Release minimind2 Series。 程式碼幾乎全部重構，使用更簡潔明瞭的統一結構。
如有舊程式碼的相容性需要，可訪問 🔗舊倉庫內容🔗 。 免去資料預處理步驟。統一資料集格式，更換為 jsonl 格式杜絕資料集下載混亂的問題。 minimind2系列效果相比MiniMind-V1顯著提升。 小問題：{kv-cache寫法更標準、MoE的負載均衡loss被考慮等等} 提供模型遷移到私有資料集的訓練方案（醫療模型、自我認知樣例）。 精簡預訓練資料集，並大幅提升預訓練資料質量，大幅縮短個人快速訓練所需時間，單卡3090即可2小時復現！ 更新：LoRA微調脫離peft包裝，從0實現LoRA過程；DPO演算法從0使用PyTorch原生實現；模型白盒蒸餾原生實現。 minimind2-DeepSeek-R1系列蒸餾模型誕生！ minimind2具備一定的英文能力！ 更新minimind2與第三方模型的基於更多大模型榜單測試效能的結果。 2024-10-05 為MiniMind拓展了多模態能力之---視覺 移步孿生專案 minimind-v 檢視詳情！ 2024-09-27 09-27更新pretrain資料集的預處理方式，為了保證文本完整性，放棄預處理成.bin訓練的形式（輕微犧牲訓練速度）。 目前pretrain預處理後的檔案命名為：pretrain_data.csv。 刪除了一些冗餘的程式碼。 2024-09-17 更新minimind-v1-moe模型 為了防止歧義，不再使用mistral_tokenizer分詞，全部採用自定義的minimind_tokenizer作為分詞器。 2024-09-01 更新minimind-v1 (108M)模型，採用minimind_tokenizer，預訓練輪次3 + SFT輪次10，更充分訓練，效能更強。 專案已部署至ModelScope創空間，可以在此網站上體驗： 🔗ModelScope線上體驗🔗 2024-08-27 專案首次開源 📌 快速開始 本人的軟硬體配置（供參考） CPU: Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10980XE CPU @ 3.00GHz RAM: 128 GB GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (24GB) * 8 Ubuntu==20.04 CUDA==12.2 Python==3.10.16 requirements.txt 第0步 # 克隆倉庫、安裝依賴 git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/jingyaogong/minimind cd minimind && pip install -r requirements.txt -i https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple Ⅰ 🚀 模型推理 1' 下載模型 在專案根目錄： # 方式1 modelscope download --model gongjy/minimind-3 --local_dir ./minimind-3 # 方式2 git clone https://huggingface.co/jingyaogong/minimind-3 2' CLI 推理 # 方式1：使用 Transformers 格式模型 python eval_llm.py --load_from ./minimind-3 # 方式2：基於 PyTorch 模型（確保./out目錄下有對應權重） python eval_llm.py --load_from ./model --weight full_sft 3'（可選）WebUI # 可能需要`python>=3.10`，安裝 `pip install streamlit` # ⚠️ 須先將 transformers 格式模型資料夾複製到 ./scripts/ 目錄下（例如：cp -r minimind-3 ./scripts/minimind-3），web_demo 指令碼會自動掃描該目錄下包含權重檔案的子資料夾，如不存在則報錯 cd scripts && streamlit run web_demo.py 4'（可選）第三方推理框架 # ollama ollama run jingyaogong/minimind-3 # vllm vllm serve /path/to/model --served-model-name " minimind " Ⅱ 🛠️ 模型訓練 注：提前確認 Torch 的可用後端 import torch print ( torch . cuda . is_available ()) 若你計劃使用 CUDA 訓練，建議先確認當前環境是否已正確識別 GPU。 若 cuda 不可用，也仍可根據自身裝置選擇 CPU 或 MPS 執行，但訓練速度與相容性會有非常大的差異。 如需安裝或更換 PyTorch 版本，可參考 torch_stable 與 連結 1' 下載資料 從下文提供的 資料集下載連結 下載所需資料檔案，並放入 ./dataset 目錄 當前預設僅需下載 pretrain_t2t_mini.jsonl 與 sft_t2t_mini.jsonl ，即可較快復現 MiniMind Zero 對話模型。
如有更多需求，下文提供多種搭配方案，可根據自身任務目標與 GPU 資源靈活選擇。 2' 開始訓練 💡 檢查點暫停續訓 所有訓練指令碼均支援檢查點儲存。新增 --from_resume 1 參數後，即可自動檢測並恢復訓練進度： python train_pretrain.py --from_resume 1
python train_full_sft.py --from_resume 1 # ... 斷點續訓說明： 訓練過程會自動在 ./checkpoints/ 目錄儲存完整檢查點（模型、最佳化器、訓練進度等） 檢查點檔案命名： <權重名>_<維度>_resume.pth （如： full_sft_512_resume.pth ） 支援跨不同 GPU 數量恢復（自動調整 step） 支援 wandb 訓練記錄連續性（自動恢復同一個 run） 適合長時間訓練或不穩定環境，無需擔心訓練中斷導致進度丟失 2.1 預訓練（必須） cd trainer && python train_pretrain.py 訓練後，將得到 out/pretrain_*.pth 作為輸出權重（其中 * 為模型 dimension，預設為 768 ） 2.2 指令微調（必須） cd trainer && python train_full_sft.py 訓練後，將得到 out/full_sft_*.pth 作為輸出權重（其中 full 表示全參數微調） 2.3 測試已訓練模型（可選） 確保待測試的模型 *.pth 檔案位於 ./out/ 目錄下；也可直接前往 此處 下載我已訓練好的 *.pth 權重。 python eval_llm.py --weight full_sft --weight 用於指定權重名稱字首，例如 pretrain 、 full_sft 等；更多參數可直接參考 eval_llm.py 注：其它須知 1、所有訓練指令碼均基於 PyTorch 原生實現，並支援多卡加速。 2、若你的裝置有 N (N > 1) 張顯示卡，可通過以下方式啟動單機 N 卡訓練（DDP，也支援擴展到多機多卡）： torchrun --nproc_per_node N train_xxx.py 3、可根據需要開啟 wandb 記錄訓練過程。 ... train_xxx.py --use_wandb 2025 年 6 月後，國內網路環境通常無法直連 WandB。MiniMind 當前預設轉為使用 SwanLab 作為訓練視覺化工具，其介面與 WandB 基本相容；通常只需將 import wandb 替換為 import swanlab as wandb ，其餘呼叫方式基本無需改動。 📌 資料介紹 Ⅰ Tokenizer 分詞器可以粗略理解成 LLM 使用的一本“詞典”，負責把自然語言對映成 token id，再把 token id 解碼迴文本；專案中也提供了 train_tokenizer.py 作為詞表訓練示例。不建議重新訓練 tokenizer，因為詞表和切分規則一旦變化，模型權重、資料格式、推理介面與社群生態的相容性都會下降，也會削弱模型的傳播性。同時，tokenizer 還會影響 PPL 這類按 token 統計的指標，因此跨 tokenizer 比較時，BPB（Bits Per Byte）往往更有參考價值，可參考 這篇 。
對 MiniMind 這類小模型來說，詞表大小還會直接影響 embedding 層和輸出層的參數佔比，因此保持詞表精簡通常是更合適的取捨。

title: anthropics/claude-code-security-review
abstract:
Claude Code Security Reviewer An AI-powered security review GitHub Action using Claude to analyze code changes for security vulnerabilities. This action provides intelligent, context-aware security analysis for pull requests using Anthropic's Claude Code tool for deep semantic security analysis. See our blog post here for more details. Features AI-Powered Analysis : Uses Claude's advanced reasoning to detect security vulnerabilities with deep semantic understanding Diff-Aware Scanning : For PRs, only analyzes changed files PR Comments : Automatically comments on PRs with security findings Contextual Understanding : Goes beyond pattern matching to understand code semantics Language Agnostic : Works with any programming language False Positive Filtering : Advanced filtering to reduce noise and focus on real vulnerabilities Quick Start Add this to your repository's .github/workflows/security.yml : name : Security Review permissions : pull-requests : write # Needed for leaving PR comments contents : read on : pull_request : jobs : security : runs-on : ubuntu-latest steps :
      - uses : actions/checkout@v4 with : ref : ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }} fetch-depth : 2 - uses : anthropics/claude-code-security-review@main with : comment-pr : true claude-api-key : ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_API_KEY }} Security Considerations This action is not hardened against prompt injection attacks and should only be used to review trusted PRs. We recommend configuring your repository to use the "Require approval for all external contributors" option to ensure workflows only run after a maintainer has reviewed the PR. Configuration Options Action Inputs Input Description Default Required claude-api-key Anthropic Claude API key for security analysis. Note : This API key needs to be enabled for both the Claude API and Claude Code usage. None Yes comment-pr Whether to comment on PRs with findings true No upload-results Whether to upload results as artifacts true No exclude-directories Comma-separated list of directories to exclude from scanning None No claude-model Claude model name to use. Defaults to Opus 4.1. claude-opus-4-1-20250805 No claudecode-timeout Timeout for ClaudeCode analysis in minutes 20 No run-every-commit Run ClaudeCode on every commit (skips cache check). Warning: May increase false positives on PRs with many commits. false No false-positive-filtering-instructions Path to custom false positive filtering instructions text file None No custom-security-scan-instructions Path to custom security scan instructions text file to append to audit prompt None No Action Outputs Output Description findings-count Total number of security findings results-file Path to the results JSON file How It Works Architecture claudecode/
├── github_action_audit.py  # Main audit script for GitHub Actions
├── prompts.py              # Security audit prompt templates
├── findings_filter.py      # False positive filtering logic
├── claude_api_client.py    # Claude API client for false positive filtering
├── json_parser.py          # Robust JSON parsing utilities
├── requirements.txt        # Python dependencies
├── test_*.py               # Test suites
└── evals/                  # Eval tooling to test CC on arbitrary PRs Workflow PR Analysis : When a pull request is opened, Claude analyzes the diff to understand what changed Contextual Review : Claude examines the code changes in context, understanding the purpose and potential security implications Finding Generation : Security issues are identified with detailed explanations, severity ratings, and remediation guidance False Positive Filtering : Advanced filtering removes low-impact or false positive prone findings to reduce noise PR Comments : Findings are posted as review comments on the specific lines of code Security Analysis Capabilities Types of Vulnerabilities Detected Injection Attacks : SQL injection, command injection, LDAP injection, XPath injection, NoSQL injection, XXE Authentication & Authorization : Broken authentication, privilege escalation, insecure direct object references, bypass logic, session flaws Data Exposure : Hardcoded secrets, sensitive data logging, information disclosure, PII handling violations Cryptographic Issues : Weak algorithms, improper key management, insecure random number generation Input Validation : Missing validation, improper sanitization, buffer overflows Business Logic Flaws : Race conditions, time-of-check-time-of-use (TOCTOU) issues Configuration Security : Insecure defaults, missing security headers, permissive CORS Supply Chain : Vulnerable dependencies, typosquatting risks Code Execution : RCE via deserialization, pickle injection, eval injection Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) : Reflected, stored, and DOM-based XSS False Positive Filtering The tool automatically excludes a variety of low-impact and false positive prone findings to focus on high-impact vulnerabilities: Denial of Service vulnerabilities Rate limiting concerns Memory/CPU exhaustion issues Generic input validation without proven impact Open redirect vulnerabilities The false positive filtering can also be tuned as needed for a given project's security goals. Benefits Over Traditional SAST Contextual Understanding : Understands code semantics and intent, not just patterns Lower False Positives : AI-powered analysis reduces noise by understanding when code is actually vulnerable Detailed Explanations : Provides clear explanations of why something is a vulnerability and how to fix it Adaptive Learning : Can be customized with organization-specific security requirements Installation & Setup GitHub Actions Follow the Quick Start guide above. The action handles all dependencies automatically. Local Development To run the security scanner locally against a specific PR, see the evaluation framework documentation . Claude Code Integration: /security-review Command By default, Claude Code ships a /security-review slash command that provides the same security analysis capabilities as the GitHub Action workflow, but integrated directly into your Claude Code development environment. To use this, simply run /security-review to perform a comprehensive security review of all pending changes. Customizing the Command The default /security-review command is designed to work well in most cases, but it can also be customized based on your specific security needs. To do so: Copy the security-review.md file from this repository to your project's .claude/commands/ folder. Edit security-review.md to customize the security analysis. For example, you could add additional organization-specific directions to the false positive filtering instructions. Custom Scanning Configuration It is also possible to configure custom scanning and false positive filtering instructions, see the docs/ folder for more details. Testing Run the test suite to validate functionality: cd claude-code-security-review # Run all tests pytest claudecode -v Support For issues or questions: Open an issue in this repository Check the GitHub Actions logs for debugging information License MIT License - see LICENSE file for details.

Overview vLLM Ascend ( vllm-ascend ) is a community maintained hardware plugin for running vLLM seamlessly on the Huawei Ascend NPU. It is the recommended approach for supporting the Ascend backend within the vLLM community. It adheres to the principles outlined in the [RFC]: Hardware pluggable , providing a hardware-pluggable interface that decouples the integration of the Ascend NPU with vLLM. By using vLLM Ascend plugin, popular open-source models, including Transformer-like, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), Embedding, Multi-modal LLMs can run seamlessly on the Ascend NPU. For detailed information on supported models and features, please refer to the Support Matrix . DeepWiki DeepWiki is a dynamic knowledge base collaboratively maintained by the community and AI, designed to provide you with deeper technical insights beyond conventional documentation. If official documentation serves as a "quick start" guide to help you get going, the DeepWiki is your technical companion for "deep understanding". Here, you can explore: core architecture and design principles, key source code interpretations, technical context, and decision-making logic. Whether you are a performance tuner looking to deploy vllm-ascend in production or a contributor aiming to build upon it for secondary development, DeepWiki offers invaluable references for you. Welcome to explore now and join us in delving deep into the technical core of vLLM-Ascend. Prerequisites Hardware: Atlas 800I A2 series, Atlas 800I A3 series, Atlas 300I Duo, 950PR&950DT Products OS: Linux Software: Python == 3.12 CANN == 9.2.1 (For Ascend HDK version, please refer to the Release Notes ) PyTorch == 2.10.0, TorchNPU == 2.10.0.post7 vLLM (the same version as vllm-ascend) Accessing Ascend NPU If you need to access Ascend NPU computing resources for development or testing, please visit the HiDevLab - Online Development page on the HiDevLab platform to apply for and use them. Getting Started Please use the following recommended versions to get started quickly: Version Release type Doc v0.30.0 Latest stable version See QuickStart and Installation for more details v0.23.0 Stable version See QuickStart and Installation for more details Branch vllm-ascend has a main branch and a dev branch. main : main branch, corresponds to the vLLM main branch, and is continuously monitored for quality through Ascend CI. releases/vX.Y.Z : development branch, created alongside new releases of vLLM. For example, releases/v0.13.0 is the dev branch for vLLM v0.13.0 version. title: Dodaios/Dodaios
abstract:
Dodaios Your chief of staff for coding agents. Install · Your plans · Documentation · Website · Discord · 簡體中文 · 日本語 · Español · हिन्दी · العربية · Français · বাংলা · Português (Brasil) · Русский · Bahasa Indonesia You have Claude Code in one terminal, Codex in another, and a chat tab where
you copy plans back and forth. Dodaios ends that. It is a layer above all your
coding agents: you say what you want, by voice or chat, and one assistant takes
it from there. It writes the brief, launches the right agent in its built-in
Agentic IDE, keeps watch while it works and tells you when it's done or needs
you. Run five agents at once and still know exactly what each one did. Open source, and it runs on your computer. Works with your Claude or ChatGPT
subscription, with API keys for Claude, OpenAI and Gemini, or with local Ollama
models. 8537db20-3fb6-44ec-92f4-879eb32acb08.mp4 A real recording at 60 frames a second, played at the speed it was filmed; the waits for the models are cut out. It was recorded with Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Opus 5.5 through Claude Code. The code change, test runs and commit are real. Watch the video (MP4, 42 s, 2.5 MB) Install macOS and Linux: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Dodaios/Dodaios/main/install/install.sh | bash Windows, in PowerShell: irm https: // raw.githubusercontent.com / Dodaios / Dodaios / main / install / install.ps1 | iex The installer sets up its own Python environment, adds a launcher and opens
the app. On the first start you give the assistant a name (it is also the
wake word), connect one model and choose how you want to talk to it. For
coding work, install at least one coding agent, such as Claude Code or Codex,
and sign in to it. dodaios # start the desktop app dodaios update # install the newest release Desktop installers, pipx and servers Download the installer for your system from the latest release: Windows macOS Linux Dodaios-Setup-x64.exe Apple Silicon · Intel AppImage, x86_64 Each release lists the checksums in installers-SHA256SUMS.txt . The
installers are not signed yet: Windows shows a warning, and macOS asks you to
allow the app once in System Settings, under Privacy & Security. The code signing policy says where that stands. With pipx you get the smaller server package, without a desktop launcher. On a
Linux server without a screen, the installer takes --headless , and dodaios serve starts only the browser interface: pipx install dodaios
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Dodaios/Dodaios/main/install/install.sh | bash -s -- --headless
dodaios serve # browser interface only, for a server without a screen Dodaios runs on 64-bit Windows, macOS and glibc-based Linux. The terminal
installer works on x86-64 and Arm64 and needs Python 3.11 to 3.14 and Git; it
fetches a missing Python and offers to install a missing Git. A graphics card
is optional. So far only Windows 11 has a recorded live sign-off. Install guide · Platform support · Running it on a server Your plans and keys Dodaios costs nothing: no Dodaios account, no paid tier. It sells no model
access and never signs in for you. It starts each coding agent's official
command-line tool, and you sign in to each one yourself, so the agents run on
the plans and keys you already have. Claude Code, for example, needs a paid
Claude plan. Your use of each service follows that service's own terms. Providers and API keys Good to know Your data. Chats, memory, documents and settings are files on the
computer that runs Dodaios. A model or a connected service gets what it
needs for its part of a request. Signing in to the Google, Slack or Figma
plugin goes through a small token service that the project runs. Privacy and local data Asking first. A new chat starts at Bypass permissions, where nothing
asks. Pick an asking mode and the four hard limits above always wait for
your yes. Safety and approvals Not finished. Phone calls need your own Twilio number and are an early
preview. Most plugins still carry a Preview badge. The phone app is a web
app that your computer serves. Documentation The feature tour shows every part on one page, with pictures. The same guides are in the app
under Docs , with search. First-run setup · Troubleshooting · Architecture Contributing Fixes, tests, platform reports and documentation are welcome. The contributing guide gets you from a fork to a passing check in about ten minutes. Questions and
ideas go to Discord . Thanks to everyone who has shipped something here: License Apache License 2.0 ,
with the attribution in NOTICE . The name and
the logo are covered by the trademark policy .
Dodaios is an independent project: the products it works with belong to their
makers, and supporting a tool does not mean its maker approves of Dodaios.
Until October 2026 it was called Personal Jarvis
( why the name changed ).
Sponsors are in SPONSORS.md .

~ ch10 即可安裝對應章節： # 推薦：使用提交到倉庫的 uv.lock，獲得可復現的章節環境 uv sync --locked --extra ch1 # 未安裝 uv 時：使用 pip 從 pyproject.toml 重新解析 python -m pip install -e " .[ch1] " 執行會呼叫模型的實驗前，請按該實驗 README 配置憑據：支援根目錄配置的實驗可複製 安裝時也可直接執行：python chapter1/context/main.py uv 安裝方法見 官方文件 ； pip 仍受支援，但不會使用鎖檔案。 各實驗現有的 requirements.txt 在遷移期間繼續有效，適合只執行單個專案或需要特殊版本約束的情況。 all 是不含本地訓練棧的 CPU 友好組合，並不代表每個實驗； uv sync 每次都會精確同步當前選擇，使用特殊 extra 時請合併到同一條命令，例如 uv sync --locked --extra ch2 --extra vllm 或 uv sync --locked --extra ch7 --extra unsloth ；pip 對應為 python -m pip install -e ".[ch2,vllm]" 。 瀏覽器、CUDA、FFmpeg、Ollama、Playwright 瀏覽器及外部倉庫等系統依賴，請繼續參考各實驗 README。第 8 章部分內建第三方元件需要 Python 3.12+。 🔑 API 金鑰 建議申請下面幾個平臺的 API Key 方便學習。模型選型可參考 這篇指南 。 平臺 連結 特色 訪問節點 Kimi （月之暗面） https://platform.moonshot.cn/ Kimi 系列，Coding、Agent 能力強 中國大陸 智譜 https://openrouter.ai/ 一站式訪問全球及國內主流模型（GPT、Claude、Gemini、Kimi、GLM、DeepSeek、Qwen 等） 全球 ❓ 常見問題 Q：有 PDF / EPUB 嗎？需要自己編譯嗎？ 不需要。 電子書 一節列出了 15 種語言的 PDF / EPUB 下載連結，始終指向 main 分支的最新構建；也可以 線上閱讀 。只有想修改書稿並重新排版時才需要自行編譯。 Q：閱讀本書需要哪些前置知識？ 引言的“前置知識”一節有完整說明：能讀懂並修改中等複雜度的 Python 程式碼；用過 ChatGPT、Claude 等 LLM 產品；熟悉至少一款 AI 輔助程式設計工具（Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 等）；瞭解命令列、Git、JSON、REST API 等軟體工程常識。除第八章後訓練外，全書對數學和機器學習的要求很低。 Q：知識點多、讀完就忘，怎麼消化？ 不要只讀正文。推薦的方式是結合每章實驗自己動手——不是看配套程式碼，而是讀懂書中的設計原則後，藉助 coding agent 從頭實現一遍，觀察輸出、排查不符合預期的地方；每章末尾的思考題也是很好的自測。更系統的路徑見 學習建議 。一位讀者的總結很貼切：先把書看薄，再把書看厚，再把書看薄。 Q：實驗程式碼需要逐行弄明白嗎？ 不需要。本書的配套程式碼全部由 coding agent 根據書稿生成，作者也不會逐行閱讀。關鍵是把架構、核心元件和設計原則想清楚，然後讓 AI 去寫程式碼、跑測試、修 bug，人負責最初的設計和最終的驗收。 Q：思考題有參考答案嗎？ 有： book/reference-answers.md （ 線上版 ）。它們只是參考，不是標準答案，歡迎在 Discussions 裡討論你的不同看法。 Q：讀完之後有什麼可以落地的實踐專案？ 推薦從頭做一個像 Claude Code、Codex 那樣的 coding agent：第 1–5 章足以做出一個可用的 coding agent；第 7、9 章幫它建立評估集並從失敗案例中持續改進；第 8 章介入模型本身；第 6、10 章為它增加語音、Computer Use 等互動方式和多 Agent 協作。評測、觀測、可靠性這些工程環節，可以從第 7 章的評估實驗入手：先為自己的 agent 建一個十幾條任務的小評估集，再圍繞失敗用例做改進。 Q：哪裡提問和討論？ 書稿勘誤、實驗 bug、翻譯問題：開 Issue ，請註明章節、小節和原文句子。 閱讀疑問、思考題討論、經驗分享、資料推薦：請使用 GitHub Discussions 。 Q：發現錯誤想修改怎麼做？ 歡迎直接提 PR。中文版 book/ 是正本，其餘語言由中文同步：修改正文時只需改中文版並在 PR 裡說明，翻譯會在合併後統一同步。詳見 貢獻 。 💎 贊助商 感謝 Krill AI 贊助本專案！Krill 提供 GPT / Claude / Gemini / 多款國產模型的官方穩定極速 API 中轉服務，支援企業級定製、報銷開票、7×16h 專屬技術支援，更有獨家適配的 WebSocket 連線方式，暢享極速首字速度。 Krill 為本書讀者提供特別優惠：使用 此連結 註冊並在充值時填寫優惠碼「ai-agent-book」，首次購買 Codex 套餐可享 77 折優惠！ 🧪 配套實驗的執行狀態、證據與未完成門禁單獨記錄在 docs/EXPERIMENT_STATUS.md ；克隆或安裝原始碼不代表實驗完成。 📦 附錄 · 外部倉庫獲取 本附錄列出第 6、7、8、10 章與實驗直接對映的 22 個外部倉庫，另含 1
